endpoint and response-field tables for spp_api_v2 and six extension modules; the previous REST half (29 operations) was authored from these. Superseded by the vendor source: the docs omit whole addons (GIS, simulation, change requests, consent, studio), give no list envelope (search results were modelled as bare arrays; the source returns a {data, meta, links} SearchResult or a Bundle), and name the token endpoint /token where the router serves /oauth/token.

up to 3.x all 20 operations went through odoo-await (XML-RPC at /xmlrpc/2/common and /xmlrpc/2/object). 4.0.0 (2026-09-29) rewrote the adaptor onto the REST API v2: request() prefixes /api/v2/spp, authorize() POSTs /oauth/token, and every named operation is a GET/POST/PATCH/PUT on Individual, Group ($add-member/$remove-member), Program, ProgramMembership or ServicePoint. Checked against dist/index.cjs of 4.0.1.

notes: OpenSPP is a social-protection registry built on Odoo, and its externally reachable API has two halves, both described here. (1) OpenSPP's REST API v2 (spp_api_v2 + extension addons, FastAPI, base path /api/v2/spp). This is now the half that matters: @openfn/language-openspp 4.0.0 dropped XML-RPC and calls only /api/v2/spp/* (OAuth client-credentials at /oauth/token, then Individual, Group, $add-member/$remove-member, Program, ProgramMembership, ServicePoint), and its generic request() reaches any route here. The previous 29 REST operations were authored from the module reference pages; they are replaced by all 107 operations the API V2 app registers in the vendor source (OpenSPP/OpenSPP2 19.0 @ a71e8f04), read statically from the router modules of spp_api_v2, its ten extension addons and spp_studio_api_v2 in registration order: paths (router prefix + route), methods, Path/Query/Header parameters with their aliases (_count, _offset, _lastId, _elements, ...), defaults and bounds, request bodies, status codes (201 creates, 204 deletes), response_model schemas and bearer security from the get_authenticated_client/get_current_client dependencies. Component schemas are the Pydantic models those routes use (156), translated to OpenAPI 3.0.3 the way FastAPI would emit them (aliases as property names, Optional as nullable, Literal as enum, polymorphic_body fields as oneOf). Each operation carries x-openspp-source, the router file it came from. What this fixed beyond the 78 new operations: the token endpoint is /oauth/token (the docs-based spec said /token); searches return the SearchResult envelope {data, meta{total,count,offset}, links{self,next,prev}} (Individual, Group, Program, ProgramMembership, Cycle, Entitlement, ChangeRequest) or a Bundle (Product, ProductCategory, UnitOfMeasure, ServicePoint, the _search routes), not bare arrays; Individual/Group gain PUT and PATCH, Group gains member add/remove/update, merge, split and membership history; ProgramMembership gains PUT. Two vendor-source oddities are documented as declared, not patched: the four GET .../_filters routes are registered after GET .../{identifier} on the same prefix, so Starlette answers them with the read route (each says so); and spp_api_v2_simulation's registry imports ..routers.aggregation while the aggregation router lives in routers/analytics.py, so the five simulation routers plus /aggregation are what the addon intends to serve but would fail to load at that commit. The OAuth handler parses its own body (JSON, form-encoded or HTTP Basic), so its TokenRequest body is described by hand from _parse_token_request. Error responses are FastAPI's {detail} body as 'default'. (2) Odoo's external API, which is RPC and not REST: POST /xmlrpc/2/common and /xmlrpc/2/object (XML-RPC, text/xml) and POST /web/session/authenticate and /jsonrpc (JSON-RPC), kept unchanged with the Odoo* record schemas, because adaptor 3.x (and the openfn-mocker XML-RPC mock) still use them. BEST-EFFORT, reason rpc-transport: execute_kw dispatches model methods by name at runtime, so the RPC half is open-ended in depth and its XML wire format cannot be described. The REST half is the complete declared route table of the addons named above; a deployment serves only the addons it installs, and its own /api/v2/spp/openapi.json is the authority for that deployment.
